rows: Multiple reports of large hail ranging in size from pennies to quarters were received as a severe storm moved from rural portions of southwestern King County to Guthrie.
Severe thunderstorm winds destroyed a horse barn near Guthrie. No additional structural damage was reported.
A convenience store clerk reported three-quarter inch diameter hail in Guthrie.
A motorist reported three-quarter inch diameter hail along U.S. Highway 82 east of Guthrie.
The public reported severe thunderstorm wind gusts to at least 60 MPH. No reports of significant damage were received.
An isolated severe thunderstorm produced a microburst southwest of Guthrie. A Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site recorded a 58 mph wind gust. No damage was reported.
Large tree limbs were broken by damaging thunderstorm winds at a ranch headquarters southwest of Guthrie.

A National Weather Service cooperative observer reported that severe thunderstorm wind gusts up to 60 mph damaged tents and other lightweight objects in Guthrie. A National Weather Service survey team found large tree branches up to 5 inches in diameter that were blown down by th…
Quarter size hail was reported in Dumont.
The public reported quarter size hail in Guthrie.

The Texas Tech West Texas Mesonet site southwest of Guthrie recorded a severe thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph at 13:15 CST. The storm continued to produce severe winds as it moved eastward, passing south of Guthrie, and then along U.S. Highway 82 east of the city. A resident at …
The public reported one inch hail at a residence on the Four 6's Ranch east of Guthrie.

A local utility company reported the loss of numerous wooden utility poles as severe thunderstorms produced damaging wind gusts along swath over southeastern King County. More than fifty poles were destroyed across King and neighboring Stonewall County, but the exact number damag…
The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site southwest of Guthrie recorded a severe thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph. No damage was reported.

The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 64 mph southwest of Guthrie at 19:05 CST. By 19:22 CST, the public estimated wind gusts up to 80 mph in Guthrie. Since no damage was reported the estimated wind speed appears too high.
The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet measured a severe thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph southwest of Guthrie. No damage was reported.

A storm chaser observed a brief tornado, seen within lightning flashes and associated with utility power flashes, over rural portions of southwestern King County shortly before 22:00 CST. The tornado remained over open range land south of U.S. Highway 82 southwest of Guthrie, and…

An isolated supercell thunderstorm developed near a dryline over the eastern Rolling Plains of west Texas during the mid afternoon hours of the 26th. This storm produced a swath of large hail up to the size of half dollars along U.S. Highway 82, roughly between that highway's int…

Another round of more scattered thunderstorms developed along and east of the dryline by the late afternoon hours of the 26th. An isolated storm became severe in King County, and produced a swath of large hail up to the size of golfballs from just west of Guthrie to just north of…
Law enforcement officials reported penny size hail in Guthrie.

Newspaper accounts described a local rancher's eyewitness account of a tornado that occurred one mile north of Finney shortly before 19:30 CST. The witness stated that he observed a tornado travel a short distance across the north side of his property for about one minute before …
Multiple public and law enforcement reports of large hail that ranged in size from nickels to golfballs were received in the Guthrie vicinity.

Motorists reported that hail was sufficiently large to lightly damage a vehicle along U.S. Highway 82 east-southeast of Guthrie. The exact hail size is unknown, therefore a minimal severe size estimate is assigned here.
A Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site measured a 58 mph thunderstorm wind gust southwest of Guthrie. No damage was reported.

A National Weather Service cooperative observer reported nickel size hail near Southcamp (10 miles southwest of Guthrie) at 19:45 CST. The public additionally reported penny size hail along Farm to Market Road 222 in extreme eastern King County at 20:05 CST.
The Dickens Fire Department reported nickel size hail in Grow.
Quarter size hail was reported along Farm to Market Road 222 south of U.S. Highway 82.
A National Weather Service cooperative observer reported quarter size hail along U.S. Highway 82 west of Guthrie.
The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site southwest of Guthrie recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 58 mph. No damage was reported.

Law enforcement officials reported that half dollar to golfball size hail covered the ground in Guthrie. A few of the hail stones reportedly were as large as two inches in diameter. No significant damage was reported.

The public reported that huge hail fell on the Masterson Ranch northeast of Guthrie during the very early morning hours on the 19th. Only minor damages were reported, and the event time is estimated based on radar data.

The Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet site southwest of Guthrie initially recorded a thunderstorm wind gust of 65 mph at 23:45 CST. Additional severe gusts up to 62 mph were measured through 23:55 CST. No damage was reported.
A severe thunderstorm produced penny to quarter size hail in the Guthrie vicinity between 14:18 CST and 14:30 CST. The hail fall delayed school releases.
A National Weather Service cooperative observer reported quarter size hail west of Guthrie.
The public reported that thunderstorm winds blew over and destroyed a large chimney at a ranch house along U.S. Highway 83 south of Guthrie.

Large hail impacted the Dumont vicinity around 04:00 CST. Observers did not directly witness the hailfall, but sizable hailstones remained on the ground seven to eight hours after the storm. A National Weather Service cooperative observer reported that bark was partially removed …

A trained spotter reported estimated wind gusts to 70 mph as well as wind damage |in Dumont. The spotter reported damage to trees and roof damage to a mobile home. There was also substantial damage to a barn. Small hail also accompanied the severe winds.
An NWS cooperative weather observer reported quarter size hail. No damage was reported.
A storm chaser measured quarter size hail 12 miles east-southeast of Guthrie. No damage was reported.
A storm chaser reported a swath of tennis ball size hail along U.S. Highway 83 south of Guthrie. No damage was reported.

A right-moving supercell produced a swath of large hail at times as large as baseballs from Grow southeast to 15E Guthrie along US Highway 82. The largest hail was estimated by a NWS Cooperative Observer in Grow; however, no reports of damage were received with this hailswath.

Storm chasers in Guthrie documented large hail that grew to baseball size over the course of about two minutes as a mesocyclone tracked just north and east of the city. Although some of this hail did damage building roofs and vehicles, the majority of the damage in the city was c…

Multiple storm chasers reported scattered to widespread wind damage in the city of Guthrie from intense rear flank downdraft winds estimated near 90 mph. Several roofs in the city suffered various degrees of damage, with at least one roof partially blown off. A large equipment ga…
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet station located 10WSW Guthrie.
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet station.
A 61 mph wind gust was measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet station near Guthrie.
A cooperative observer near Dumont observed widespread pea size hail with occasional quarter size stones. No damage was reported.
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas Mesonet located 10 miles west-southwest of Guthrie.
A COOP observer reported golf ball to baseball size hail covering the ground. Several vehicles were damaged and lost windows or windshields.
A roof was blown off a well-constructed barn at the Four Sixes Ranch.
A storm chaser photographed hail around golf ball size. Damage was unknown. Time and location were estimated.

Local fire department officials and a local COOP observer reported a tornado just west of Guthrie and south of Highway 82 near the Four Sixes Ranch. Reports and documentation suggest the tornado lasted about one minute in an open field and did not produce any damage or injuries.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie reported wind gusts up to 64 mph for a five minute period.
Hail up to two inches in diameter was observed on the ground by a storm chaser. Damage was unknown.
A storm chaser estimated tennis ball size hail north of Guthrie on US Highway 83. Damage was not reported.
A second storm produced quarter size hail at the same location as the prior event. No damage was reported, but the hail was said to have completely covered the ground.
A swath of severe hail ranging from the size of quarters to hen eggs fell along a stretch of US Highway 83 north of Guthrie. Damage was not known.
The Paducah Fire Department reported quarter size hail along US Highway 83 in King County. No damage was reported.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured a wind gust to 76 mph.
This tornado developed from a cyclic supercell responsible for the previous tornado in far eastern Dickens County. No damage was reported with this tornado as it remained over open land.
Law enforcement in King County and a cooperative weather observer reported hail ranging from quarter size to golf ball size in and around Guthrie. No damage was reported.
Measured by a Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet.
A storm chaser reported hail up to golf ball size two miles south of Guthrie.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured severe wind gusts from 1920 CST through 1925 CST. The peak wind gust measured was 66 mph.

A NWS cooperative weather observer as well as numerous storm chasers reported hail up to baseball size near Grow and along US Highway 83 to the north and south of Grow. Many windshields and storm chaser vehicles were damaged.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured a wind gust to 59 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured a wind gust to 60 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured severe wind gusts at 1707 and 1708 CST. A peak wind gust of 60 mph was measured at 1708 CST.

Numerous storm chasers documented a tornado that began near the intersection of US Highway 83 and Farm to Market Road 1168. The tornado moved roughly east-southeast remaining close to Farm to Market Road 1168 and 3416 for about five miles before turning east and crossing County R…

An NWS storm survey revealed no known damage from this tornado which was documented by several storm chasers. The tornado moved over rangeland in northeastern King County before crossing into Foard County.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured a wind gust of 60 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured severe wind gusts from 0810 CST through 0828 CST. A peak wind gust of 70 mph was measured at 0818 CST.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured severe wind gusts from 1922 CST through 1928 CST. A peak wind gust of 77 mph was measured at 1922 CST.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured severe wind gusts from 2017 CST through 2038 CST. A peak wind gust of 67 mph was measured at 2034 CST.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured a wind gust to 59 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured a wind gust of 64 mph.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured severe wind gusts from 2345 CST through 2346 CST. A peak wind gust of 65 mph was measured at 2346 CST.
A storm chaser reported quarter size hail south of Guthrie along US Highway 83.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured severe wind gusts from 1413 CST through 1414 CST. A peak wind gust of 63 mph was measured at 1413 CST.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured severe wind gusts from 0112 CST through 0115 CST. A peak wind gust of 62 mph was measured at 0112 CST.

Several reports were received of a swath of hail across a portion of King County from south of Guthrie to east of Guthrie. Reported hail ranged in size from golf ball to DVD-size. No damage was reported.
A Texas Tech University West Texas mesonet site near Guthrie measured severe wind gusts from 1952 CST through 1959 CST. A peak wind gust of 67 mph was measured at 1959 CST.
Several storm chasers reported a swath of broken power poles along US Highway 83 north of Guthrie following the passage of a thunderstorm.
